decisions.q: Which layout should the lead list use?
decisions.ctx: People skim 30–50 leads a day and open only a few of them to reply.
decisions.pattern: When the options are screen designs. Show the designs side by side and line up the rows so differences read across.

options.label: Table
options.when: Skimming many leads quickly matters most

options.label: List + detail
options.cap: Pick on the left, see it on the right
options.when: Fits skimming and then replying right away

options.label: Cards
options.when: There is a lot to show, like photos and notes

decisions.same: All three keep the same search, filter and sort.

decisions.q: What should the sign-up button say?
decisions.ctx: It is the last button of the free-trial form. See each one placed on a real button.
decisions.pattern: Copy is not judged as plain text. Show it in the place it will actually appear.

options.label: Sign up
options.when: The text above the form already explains enough

options.label: Start free
options.when: Easing payment worries is the point

options.label: Finish sign-up in 3 minutes
d: 27 characters · cut off on narrow screens
options.when: The form looks long and people drop off

decisions.q: What unit should site permissions use?
decisions.ctx: Today, permission keys differ per menu inside the same group, so three places are out of sync.
decisions.more: The three places are SEO, images and channels. In each, the group's permission and the menu's permission key were set separately.
decisions.pattern: Draw structure you can't see by its size and shape. Here, the number of cells to manage is drawn as is.

options.label: 6 groups × view/edit
options.when: You want it simple and the mismatches gone

options.label: 29 menus × view/edit/send
options.when: People need different access per menu

options.label: Keep the 4 keys, fix only the mismatches
options.when: You only need to put out the urgent fire

decisions.q: How far should the work branch go?
decisions.ctx: Pushing is hard to undo, so we ask before doing it.
decisions.pattern: A check before a hard-to-undo action. Current state as number chips; options drawn as how far it goes.

options.label: Up to staging
d: One more step to production after checking
options.when: You want to look at it before it goes out

options.label: Don't push yet
d: Commits pile up and get harder to merge
options.when: You'll push once the work in progress is done

decisions.q: Which accent color should we use?
decisions.ctx: It is used on buttons, links, badges and charts. Hover an option to change the preview.
decisions.pattern: For choices that change the overall feel: colors, fonts, spacing. One big preview, with the options swapped in.

decisions.q: Pick what goes into this week.
decisions.ctx: You have 5 days. A recommended set is already selected.
decisions.pattern: A pick-several decision. The total changes as you choose, so you can see when it overflows.

items.label: Forms admin
items.sub: Create and edit forms without code

items.label: Auto DM
items.sub: Reply automatically to people who comment

decisions.ctx: Any of them is easy to change later. You can accept the recommendations in one go.
decisions.pattern: When there are several light decisions. One row each, and a way to finish them all with the recommendations.

decisions.q: How many auto DMs should go out per day?
decisions.ctx: 1,200 people are waiting for a reply. Sending more finishes sooner but raises the risk of an account restriction.
decisions.pattern: For picking a number. Move the value and the results change, so you can see where it is reasonable.
